Next step: Karthik, Ben — added you to the thread to provide the technical/controls responses Susan asked for. Susan — if you can confirm the retention window you want for prompt data (example: 30 days) that will let us draft the procurement clause.

Hi Susan — thanks for the clear questions. I'll put concrete answers below so procurement has language to work from. Short version: default behavior is conservative, and we offer contractable options for longer retention or stricter residency.

1) What is persisted by default
- Prompt inputs: by default, hosted API does not persist raw prompt inputs beyond processing unless a customer opts into "persisted logs" for debugging or quality monitoring. If persisted, inputs are stored encrypted at rest in their raw form unless the customer chooses automatic redaction. We also offer on-request hashing/pseudonymization where the raw text is replaced with salted hashes for data you want to compare but not retain in plaintext.
- Prompt outputs: default is ephemeral for streaming calls (not written to long-term storage). For non-streaming calls, a short-lived cache (service cache) may hold outputs for up to 5 minutes to support retries. Persisted output storage is opt-in and subject to contract.
- Metadata & telemetry: request metadata (timestamp, model id, token counts), request/response sizes, latency, and error traces are collected by default for observability and billing. These do not include full prompt text unless persistence is enabled.

2) Default TTLs (hosted) — concrete numbers you can use in an SOW
- Request/response payloads (when persisted by opt-in): default retention 30 days; can be extended to 90/365 days by contract.
- Inference logs (latency, errors, traces): default retention 90 days.
- Audit logs (account-level auth events, config changes): default retention 365 days for Dedicated contracts; hosted tier default 180 days. Extended retention is available as an add-on (up to 7 years).
- Short-term caches (service caches, KV caches): 5 minutes by default and not written to durable storage.

3) Residency
- Hosted: default single-tenant logical separation in region (us-east-1). We can pin your tenant to an EU region (eu-west-1) for hosted customers but note that SLA parity for certain dedicated performance SLAs is only guaranteed on Redwood Dedicated/Private.
- Dedicated/Private: full EU-only or APAC-only deployments (control plane location and data plane) are supported and contractable.

4) SOC 2 and evidence
- We are SOC 2 Type II certified; latest report date: 2026-06-01. We can provide an executive summary and a redacted SOC 2 report under an NDA.
- Pen test cadence: quarterly internal + annual third-party. Summary artifact and remediation timeline available on request. Audit artifacts are retained per contract; standard hosted customers: 1 year of retention for evidence, Dedicated: retentions per contract.

Operational controls / encryption:
- All persisted data is encrypted at rest with customer-shared KMS options for Dedicated/Private. In hosted, we use provider-managed encryption; customer-managed keys available on Dedicated.
- Access to persisted prompt data is restricted via role-based access and audited.

Suggested procurement wording (short):
"Redwood Inference will not persist raw prompt inputs or outputs in the hosted default configuration unless explicitly enabled by the customer. When enabled, persisted prompt payloads will be encrypted at rest and retained for 30 days by default. Redwood offers EU-only data residency and extended retention as contract options. SOC 2 Type II report (2026) available under NDA."

I attached the short security snapshot we referenced and a data-classification matrix to map which fields you might want redacted. Happy to refine the SOW phrasing if your procurement/legal need different language.
